name: Reactive Angioendotheliomatosis

criteria.description: Presence of intravascular proliferation of endothelial cells with occlusion of vascular lumina on skin biopsy
Erythematous to violaceous plaques or nodules with livedoid or retiform purpura predominantly on acral or trunk skin
Exclusion of other vascular proliferative or thrombotic disorders such as intravascular lymphoma or vasculitis
Identification of underlying systemic conditions such as infections, malignancies, or autoimmune diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of endothelial proliferation with characteristic clinical lesions and exclusion of mimicking conditions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on skin biopsy and clinicopathologic correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intravascular endothelial proliferation with vascular occlusion
pathognomonic.notes: Observed histologically in affected skin lesions
searchTerms: blood vessel lining overgrowth causing blockages
intravascular endothelial proliferation with vessel occlusion
abnormal vessel lining growth causing blockage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Erythematous to violaceous livedoid plaques or nodules
pathognomonic.notes: Typically on acral sites or trunk
searchTerms: red to purple skin plaques or lumps with net-like pattern
livedoid skin lesions with erythema and violaceous color
skin plaques or nodules with reddish-purple color

pathognomonic.notes: Net-like purpuric lesions indicating vascular occlusion

common.symptomName: Edema localized to affected skin areas
searchTerms: swelling limited to affected skin regions

common.notes: May be present depending on underlying cause

occasional.notes: Due to vascular compromise in nerves
searchTerms: loss of feeling in hands or feet

occasional.notes: Mild joint discomfort reported in some cases
May be secondary to underlying systemic disease

rare.notes: Rarely reported due to vascular occlusion
Due to ulceration and skin barrier disruption

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers if underlying systemic disease present
Negative autoimmune serologies unless associated condition
imaging: Skin biopsy showing intravascular endothelial proliferation
Doppler ultrasound may show vascular occlusion in affected areas
other: Association with systemic infections, malignancies, or autoimmune disorders
Resolution of lesions upon treatment of underlying condition

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of malignant lymphoid cells within vessels
Histology shows fibrin thrombi without endothelial hyperplasia

redFlags: Systemic symptoms suggestive of underlying malignancy or infection
Failure to respond to treatment of underlying condition
references: Wollina U, et al. Reactive angioendotheliomatosis: a review. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2017.
Kossard S, et al. Reactive angioendotheliomatosis: clinicopathologic study of 10 cases. Am J Dermatopathol. 1991.
